ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Objects A and B, each with a mass of $m=1\mathrm{kg}$, are attached to the two ends of a massless string. The string passes over a fixed pulley at the top of an inclined plane with an angle of $\theta{=}37^{\circ}$, which is fixed on a horizontal ground. Initially, object B is pulled to the bottom of the inclined plane, while object A is at a height of $h=1\mathrm{m}$ above the ground, as shown in the figure. If the inclined plane is sufficiently long, and friction between $B$ and the inclined plane, as well as between the string and the pulley, is negligible, the system is released from rest and allowed to move. (Take $g$ as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.)

1. The speed of object A when it lands.
2. If the connection between object B and the string breaks at the moment object A hits the ground, then the time required for object B to return to the bottom of the inclined plane from this moment onward is

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the inclined plane is fixed on the horizontal ground, and the angle of the inclined plane is marked as 37°; object B is located near the bottom of the inclined plane, and the rope goes upward along the inclined plane and passes over the fixed pulley at the top of the inclined plane; the other end of the rope vertically suspends object A, A is above the ground, and the height 1 m is marked beside it. Reasoning: The rope is inextensible, so before A lands, A's downward displacement is equal to B's upward displacement along the inclined plane, and the magnitudes of their accelerations are the same. Take A downward and B upward along the inclined plane as positive. For A: mg-T=ma; for B along the direction of the inclined plane: T-mg sin37°=ma. Adding the two equations gives mg-mg sin37°=2ma, so a=g(1-sin37°)/2. Take sin37°=0.6, g=10 m/s², obtaining a=10(1-0.6)/2=2 m/s². A falls from rest through h=1 m, so v²=2ah=2×2×1=4, v=2 m/s. At the instant A lands, B has also moved upward along the inclined plane by 1 m, with speed 2 m/s. At this time, after the rope breaks, B is acted on only by the component of gravity along the inclined plane. Taking upward along the inclined plane as positive, the acceleration is -g sin37°=-6 m/s². Let the bottom of the inclined plane be x=0, then at the instant the rope breaks, B's position and velocity are x0=1 m, v0=2 m/s, so x(t)=1+2t-3t². Let B return to the bottom x=0, obtaining 1+2t-3t²=0, namely 3t²-2t-1=0, and the positive root is t=1 s.
